articles.title: Phil Mickelson’s reps say he sought treatment for family trauma and addiction
articles.summary: Golfer has spoken of gambling issues in past. Six-time major winner has not played since March. Phil Mickelson sought treatment earlier this year for “family trauma and addiction”, his representatives confirmed to multiple outlets on Wednesday.
body: The 56-year-old golfer voluntarily entered a treatment facility and has since returned home. Mickelson’s representatives did not say when he sought treatment or how long he stayed at a facility.

TMZ was the first to report the news. The six-time major winner, who has spoken in the past about gambling addiction, withdrew from the Masters in April and several LIV Golf events this year due to a “family health matter”.

In June, Mickelson denied allegations of nonconsensual and inappropriate physical conduct with a female employee at a San Diego golf club. A report by Golf Digest claimed Mickelson was challenged on an incident mid-round and left the property soon after. His lawyer confirmed he had resigned from the Farms Golf Club amid the allegations and said he was working on recovery.

“Some of the allegations circulating about Mr Mickelson are false, and others revisit mistakes he has already acknowledged, publicly or privately,” a spokesperson for Mickelson told People magazine in June, in response to an article on golf website Skratch about alleged misconduct.

articles.title: The ultra-rich face … accountability? Manchester City and Clippers verdicts show it’s possible | Leander Schaerlaeckens
articles.summary: The sports world has accomplished a rare feat: calling out industrial-scale cheating on both sides of the Atlantic. Sign up for our free newsletter here. The first stage of billionaire exposure to accountability is vociferous denial.
body: The second is bafflement that such an earthly and proletarian problem should even be allowed to happen to you, titan of industry, pillar of society, master of man and beast alike.
The third is a milquetoast non-apology apology “for the distraction and distress this matter has caused”, after issuing a total and belligerent denial through your proxies.

Within the last month, we have traipsed, on tiptoes, into a strange new age where some modicum of repercussion may occasionally threaten the billionaire class – albeit strictly limited to the confines of sports, where nothing actually matters. It’s a new and funny feeling in an age when it seems that the 1% don’t just get a bespoke business climate, where taxation and regulation are administered on an opt-in basis, but their own concierge service from the justice system, too.
Setting aside for the moment the argument of whether billionaires should exist at all, or whether they are a flagrant failure of fiscal policy, this is a remarkable turn of events.

articles.summary: Government said to be unhappy at lack of warning. Burnham previously criticised league’s Everton sanction. Andy Burnham’s intervention in the Manchester City debate has revived tensions between the Premier League and the prime minister.
body: The Premier League published a redacted 40-page version of the commission’s report on Tuesday, not long after Burnham’s first keynote speech as leader at the Labour party conference.

Burnham responded in a series of interviews on Wednesday by saying he would be “really concerned” if City’s owners were forced to sell after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of financial rules, although he did add he could not intervene more in the process, which remains subject to appeal.

City’s disciplinary fate lies in the hands of an independent commission and pending its final judgment the owners’ suitability to remain running the club could be assessed by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), with no role for the Premier League or government.

The Times and Daily Mail have reported that City’s appeal will be based on evidence the club claim proves their sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government and not the club. The commission rejected that argument as “untrue”.

articles.title: Frustrated MacIntyre warned after drone row
articles.summary: Robert MacIntyre says the use of drones for broadcast coverage at golf tournaments "drives me insane" after being spoken to by a DP World Tour rules official at the Dunhill Links Championship.
body: Scotland's number one golfer, the defending champion, became frustrated with a drone as he approached the closing stages of his opening round at Carnoustie on Thursday.
The 30-year-old, who is ranked 19th in the world, dropped a shot at the par-four ninth - his 18th hole of the day - to finish on one under par.
MacIntyre said the noise from drones flying close to players can affect his concentration, particularly in windy conditions.

"See, when they're staying still, it's fine. It's more the buffeting from the wind and it's trying to stay in position. It's like a revving of a car right where you're trying to hit. I struggle with it.

articles.title: Houston high school football rivalry cancelled due to skin infection outbreak
articles.summary: One of Houston's biggest high school football games was canceled because of an outbreak of a contagious skin infection. Bellaire High School principal Michael Niggli sent a letter to parents stating that multiple members of the Cardinals football team were diagnosed with staph infections.
body: As a result, Friday's pivotal contest between Bellaire and the Lamar Texans at Delmar Stadium has been canceled. The canceled contest was also tabbed as Lamar's 2026 homecoming game.

"The decision is based on guidance from the HISD Health and Medical Department and the Houston Health Department Epidemiology team," Niggli said in a statement on Thursday. "HISD is taking appropriate steps in response to the confirmed cases."

According to the Cleveland Clinic, staph infection is a contagious disease caused by Staphylococcus bacteria entering the body through a cut, scrape, or other break in the skin. Managing staph is especially challenging for football teams because of constant skin-to-skin contact, high rates of nasal carriage and shared equipment.

According to Niggli, under UIL guidelines, the game will be recorded as a win for Lamar, now 3-2, giving them a three-game winning streak and their first in district play. Meanwhile, Bellaire's forfeited loss drops their record to 1-5. Next week's matchups for both clubs feature Lamar traveling to Alief Taylor on Thursday, Oct. 8, while Bellaire will host Houston Heights on Friday, Oct. 9.

articles.title: How Man City plan to argue their innocence in appeal
articles.summary: Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners.
body: An independent commission has found that City broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830.69m of owner funding as sponsorship income.
City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the commission.
In their judgement the commission "concluded that it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".
Manchester City is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Newton Investment and Development LLC.
points: Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners.

articles.title: Rashid, Curran return from injury as England rest Archer for ODI tri-series
articles.summary: Adil Rashid and Sam Curran have been recalled to England's ODI squad after recovering from injury, but Jofra Archer will be rested for the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
body: Three uncapped players are included in the 16-player squad for the series in Pakistan, which will see Harry Brook's side play each opponent twice. Spinner Mason Crane is included eight years on from making his last international appearance, which came in the final Test of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour.
Sussex duo James Coles and Henry Crocombe could also make their ODI debuts having been included after being part of England's white-ball squads earlier this summer.
Rashid featured as England beat Sri Lanka in a home T20 series in September but the spinner then missed the ODI matches that followed because of a hand injury.
Curran had appeared to be in contention for a first Test appearance since 2021 before his summer was ended by groin surgery in August, but the all-rounder is on track to be ready to play in Pakistan.
